# `iw` — the world format

*Structure generated from the source by `reference.py`; the explanations come from `reference_notes.py`. Do not edit this file -- edit those and re-run.*

`iw` is a small, dependency-free Python library that mirrors the game engine's world-definition JSON as
typed dataclasses, and serializes them to and from that JSON. Use it to build world definitions
programmatically, or to read and round-trip existing ones. It depends only on the standard library and is
fully standalone — it does **not** require [`plot`](plot.md).

This page is **every object in `iw`, every attribute on it, and every enum member** — what each one is,
what it is for, and how it is used. The structure is read out of the dataclasses themselves, so it cannot
fall behind the library; the explanations sit beside it rather than in a separate document.

A field you never set gets the default shown, and a default the engine is happy with — so in practice you
name only the handful you care about.

```python
import iw
```

A world is an `iw.World`. It holds content (characters, NPCs, instruction blocks, lorebook entries,
tracked items, image/style settings) plus an **event system** (`triggerEvents`) that drives dynamic
behaviour. You assemble a `World` from the dataclasses below and call `.to_json()` to get the engine's
JSON; or parse engine JSON back with `World.from_json()`.

### `VictoryDefeatCondition`

| attribute | type | default | what it's for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `condition` | `str` | `required` | What must happen, judged by the AI. |

### `InitialTrackedItemValue`

| attribute | type | default | what it's for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `str` | `required` | The id of the tracked item this value is for. |
| `name` | `str` | `required` | That item's name, repeated. |
| `initialPCValue` | `str \| list[str]` | `''` | This character's starting value — or a list of options to choose between. |
| `visibility` | `TrackedItemVisibility` | `TrackedItemVisibility.AI_ONLY` | Who can see it, for this character. |
| `initialValueBasedOnPC` | `TrackedItemInitialValueSource` | `TrackedItemInitialValueSource.CHARACTER` | Mirrors the item's own mode; an entry declaring anything but `CHARACTER` is dropped on import. |
| `initialPCValueChoicesScript` | `Optional[str]` | `None` | A `$`-script yielding this character's options. |

One of these exists per character for each `CHARACTER`-mode tracked item — they are not free-form
overrides you attach at will. See [Initial values](#initial-values-same--character--player).

### `TrackedItem`

| attribute | type | default | what it's for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `str` | `required` | What the player sees in the tracked-item panel. |
| `id` | `str` | `auto` | The id triggers refer to it by. Never write one by hand. |
| `dataType` | `TrackedItemDataType` | `TrackedItemDataType.TEXT` | Whether the value is text, a number, or a structured document. |
| `visibility` | `TrackedItemVisibility` | `TrackedItemVisibility.EVERYONE` | Who can see it. |
| `description` | `str` | `''` | What this item means, for the AI's benefit. |
| `updateInstructions` | `str` | `''` | How the AI should decide to change it. |
| `initialValue` | `str` | `''` | The starting value, for `SAME` and `PLAYER` modes. |
| `initialValueBasedOnPC` | `TrackedItemInitialValueSource` | `TrackedItemInitialValueSource.SAME` | Where the starting value comes from. |
| `autoUpdate` | `bool` | `False` | Lets the AI update the item on its own each turn. |
| `variableName` | `Optional[str]` | `None` | The item's `$`-script handle. Derived from the name if unset — and kept when the item is renamed, so the two can diverge. |
| `enforceFormat` | `Optional[bool]` | `None` | Requires the value to match `formatSchema`. |
| `formatSchema` | `Optional[str]` | `None` | The schema a structured value must satisfy. |
| `formatExample` | `Optional[str]` | `None` | A worked example of the expected format. |
| `driftAcknowledgedForName` | `Optional[str]` | `None` | Engine bookkeeping for a name that has drifted from its handle. |
| `initialValueChoices` | `Optional[list[str]]` | `None` | For `PLAYER` mode: the literal options the player picks between. |
| `initialValueChoicesScript` | `Optional[str]` | `None` | For `PLAYER` mode: a `$`-script yielding those options. |

`item.variable_name` is the item's handle — its `variableName` if one is set, otherwise the name
lowercased with spaces → underscores. A **renamed item keeps its original handle**, so it is this, not the
visible `name`, that a `$`-script or a substitution refers to. `item.as_substitution()` wraps it as
`<<…>>` for embedding in trigger and instruction text.

Where an item's starting value comes from is a whole topic of its own — see
[Initial values](#initial-values-same--character--player) below.

### `TriggerEffect`

| attribute | type | default | what it's for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | `EffectType` | `required` | Which kind of effect. |
| `data` | `Any` | `required` | The payload. Its shape depends on `type` — see the effect tables. |
| `id` | `str` | `auto` | Its own id. |
| `trackedItemID` | `Optional[str]` | `None` | The item written, repeated outside `data` — both copies must agree. |

The engine fills in extra keys on some payloads that you do not have to write: `path`, `updateMode`,
`listExpression` and `targetExpression` on `SET_TRACKED_ITEM_VALUE`, `path`/`updateMode` on
`PRESENT_CHOICE` and `REQUEST_INPUT`, and `alreadyFired` on a victory/defeat condition.

### `TriggerCondition`

| attribute | type | default | what it's for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data` | `Any` | `required` | The payload. Its shape depends on `type` — see the condition table. |
| `id` | `str` | `auto` | Its own id. |
| `type` | `Optional[ConditionType]` | `None` | Which kind of condition. Absent on a logic group. |
| `category` | `Optional[str]` | `None` | `"condition"` for a leaf, `"logic"` for a group. |
| `trackedItemID` | `Optional[str]` | `None` | The item read, repeated outside `data` — both copies must agree. |
| `inequality` | `Optional[Inequality]` | `None` | The comparison, written here as well as in `data`, and only when it is not the default. |
| `operator` | `Optional[LogicOperator]` | `None` | `AND` / `OR`, on a logic group. |

Set either a `type` (a leaf condition) or `category="logic"` with an `operator` (a group combining
sub-conditions). A group's `data` holds `TriggerCondition`s whether you built the group or parsed one —
a parsed group's raw sub-dicts are built out on construction — and the owning `TriggerEvent` needs
`advancedLogic=True`. Every leaf condition carries `category="condition"`; the helpers set it for you.

| `advancedLogic` | `Optional[bool]` | `None` | Required before a condition may be a logic group. |
| `triggerOnStartOfGame` | `Optional[bool]` | `None` | Fires once, before the first turn. |
| `canTriggerMoreThanOnce` | `Optional[bool]` | `None` | Lets it fire again; otherwise it fires once ever. |

- `world.to_dict()` / `world.to_json()` — emit the engine JSON. Optional fields are omitted while still
  at their default, and `positionInList` is stamped onto tracked items and NPCs.
- `iw.World.from_dict(data)` / `iw.World.from_json(s)` — parse engine JSON back into dataclasses. Parsing
  is **strict**: an unknown field raises `NotImplementedError`, so the dataclasses stay a faithful mirror
  of the schema.
- `world.validate()` — raise `ValueError` listing everything that doesn't hang together. **`to_json()`
  calls this for you**, so a broken world raises instead of becoming a file.
- `world.summary()` — a readable account of what is in the world. Print it before and after a change.

The dangling-reference case is worth dwelling on, because it is the one that bites. Triggers name their
tracked items, blocks and characters **by id**. If a trigger holds an id nothing answers to any more, the
engine loads the world perfectly happily — and then that trigger simply never fires. Nothing tells you.
You find it by playing. So the library refuses to write that file at all.

## The enums

Every one is a `StrEnum`, so a member *is* the string the engine reads — you can pass the member or its value and the JSON comes out the same. Prefer the member: a typo in a member name is an `AttributeError`, and a typo in a string is a world that loads and quietly does nothing.

The examples below all run, and refer to these:

```python
mood    = iw.TrackedItem(name="Mood", initialValue="calm")
crew    = iw.TrackedItem(name="Crew", dataType=iw.TrackedItemDataType.NUMBER, initialValue="4")
roster  = iw.TrackedItem(name="Roster", dataType=iw.TrackedItemDataType.YAML)
rules   = iw.InstructionBlock(name="Rules", content="Be terse.")
dragons = iw.LoreBookEntry(name="Dragons", content="They sleep.", keywords=["dragon"])
ambush  = iw.TriggerEvent(name="Ambush")
storm   = iw.TriggerEvent(name="Storm")
hero    = iw.PossibleCharacter(name="Hero")
```

### `TrackedItemDataType`

| member | value in the JSON | what it does | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TEXT` | `text` | A plain string. The default. | `iw.TrackedItem(name="Mood", dataType=iw.TrackedItemDataType.TEXT, initialValue="calm")` |
| `NUMBER` | `number` | A number, still carried as a string. | `iw.TrackedItem(name="Crew", dataType=iw.TrackedItemDataType.NUMBER, initialValue="4")` |
| `XML` | `xml` | Structured data as XML. Semi-deprecated — prefer `YAML`. | `iw.TrackedItem(name="Party", dataType=iw.TrackedItemDataType.XML)` |
| `YAML` | `yaml` | Structured data as a YAML document: nested maps and lists, reachable from `$`-scripts. The going-forward type. | `iw.TrackedItem(name="Roster", dataType=iw.TrackedItemDataType.YAML, initialValue="members:\n  - name: Ivo")` |

### `TrackedItemVisibility`

| member | value in the JSON | what it does | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `EVERYONE` | `everyone` | Shown to the player and given to the AI. | `iw.TrackedItem(name="Mood", visibility=iw.TrackedItemVisibility.EVERYONE)` |
| `AI_ONLY` | `ai_only` | Given to the AI, never shown to the player. | `iw.TrackedItem(name="Suspicion", visibility=iw.TrackedItemVisibility.AI_ONLY)` |
| `PLAYER_ONLY` | `player_only` | Shown to the player, withheld from the AI. | `iw.TrackedItem(name="Notes", visibility=iw.TrackedItemVisibility.PLAYER_ONLY)` |
| `HIDDEN` | `hidden` | Hidden in normal play; visible in storyteller mode. | `iw.TrackedItem(name="Stage", visibility=iw.TrackedItemVisibility.HIDDEN)` |
| `HIDDEN_BORING` | `hidden_boring` | Hidden in normal play; visible only in debug mode. | `iw.TrackedItem(name="Turn counter", visibility=iw.TrackedItemVisibility.HIDDEN_BORING)` |

`HIDDEN` and `HIDDEN_BORING` both hide an item from the player in normal play; the difference is *where*
it still shows. `HIDDEN` is visible in **storyteller mode**, `HIDDEN_BORING` only in **debug mode**. Reach
for `HIDDEN_BORING` for bookkeeping the storyteller never needs to see.

### `TrackedItemInitialValueSource`

| member | value in the JSON | what it does | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SAME` | `same` | Every playthrough starts from the item's own `initialValue`. | `iw.TrackedItem(name="Mood", initialValueBasedOnPC=iw.TrackedItemInitialValueSource.SAME, initialValue="calm")` |
| `CHARACTER` | `character` | The value depends on which character is chosen, and lives on each character. | `iw.TrackedItem(name="Homeland", initialValueBasedOnPC=iw.TrackedItemInitialValueSource.CHARACTER)` |
| `PLAYER` | `player` | The player enters it; `initialValue` is the default they edit. | `iw.TrackedItem(name="Callsign", initialValueBasedOnPC=iw.TrackedItemInitialValueSource.PLAYER, initialValue="Nomad")` |

Which mode an item is in decides *where its starting value lives* — see
[Initial values](#initial-values-same--character--player) below.

### `TrackedItemAction`

| member | value in the JSON | what it does | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SET` | `set` | Overwrite the value. | `set_tracked_item(mood, "uneasy")` |
| `ADD` | `add` | Add to it. | `set_tracked_item(crew, "1", action=iw.TrackedItemAction.ADD)` |
| `SUBTRACT` | `subtract` | Take away from it. | `set_tracked_item(crew, "1", action=iw.TrackedItemAction.SUBTRACT)` |
| `REPLACE` | `replace` | Find `newValue` and swap in `replaceWith` — here the value you pass is the needle, not the result. | `set_tracked_item(mood, "calm", action=iw.TrackedItemAction.REPLACE)` |

### `Inequality`

| member | value in the JSON | what it does | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `IS_EXACTLY` | `is_exactly` | Equal. The default, and the one the engine does not write down. | `tracked_item_is(mood, "uneasy")` |
| `AT_LEAST` | `at_least` | Greater than or equal. | `tracked_item_is(crew, "2", inequality=iw.Inequality.AT_LEAST)` |
| `AT_MOST` | `at_most` | Less than or equal. | `tracked_item_is(crew, "2", inequality=iw.Inequality.AT_MOST)` |
| `NOT_EQUAL` | `not_equal` | Different. | `tracked_item_is(mood, "calm", inequality=iw.Inequality.NOT_EQUAL)` |

### `EffectType`

| member | value in the JSON | what it does | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SHOW_MESSAGE` | `effectShowMessage` | Shows the player a message, outside the narration. | `iw.TriggerEffect(type=iw.EffectType.SHOW_MESSAGE, data="The bridge collapses behind you.")` |
| `GIVE_INFO` | `effectGiveInfo` | Tells the AI something out of band, without narrating it. | `iw.TriggerEffect(type=iw.EffectType.GIVE_INFO, data="The captain is lying about the cargo.")` |
| `TELL_AI` | `effectTellAIWhatToDo` | Instructs the AI on what to do next. | `iw.TriggerEffect(type=iw.EffectType.TELL_AI, data="Raise the tension. End the scene on a threat.")` |
| `CHANGE_MAIN_INSTRUCTIONS` | `effectChangeMainInstructions` | Rewrites the main instructions. | `iw.TriggerEffect(type=iw.EffectType.CHANGE_MAIN_INSTRUCTIONS, data="I am now the hunted, not the hunter.")` |
| `MODIFY_INSTRUCTION_BLOCK` | `effectModifyInstructionBlock` | Rewrites a block's text. | `iw.TriggerEffect(type=iw.EffectType.MODIFY_INSTRUCTION_BLOCK, data={"id": rules.id, "content": "Be terse. Never explain the magic."})` |
| `CHANGE_AUTHOR_STYLE` | `effectChangeAuthorStyle` | Rewrites the author-style voice. | `iw.TriggerEffect(type=iw.EffectType.CHANGE_AUTHOR_STYLE, data="Terse, clipped, hard-boiled.")` |
| `CHANGE_DESCRIPTION_INSTRUCTIONS` | `effectChangeDescriptionInstructions` | Rewrites the description-request instructions. | `iw.TriggerEffect(type=iw.EffectType.CHANGE_DESCRIPTION_INSTRUCTIONS, data="Describe each scene in two sentences, no more.")` |
| `CHANGE_OBJECTIVE` | `effectChangeObjective` | Rewrites the on-screen goal. | `iw.TriggerEffect(type=iw.EffectType.CHANGE_OBJECTIVE, data="Escape the city before dawn.")` |
| `CHANGE_BACKGROUND` | `effectChangeBackground` | Rewrites the background. | `iw.TriggerEffect(type=iw.EffectType.CHANGE_BACKGROUND, data="A drowned city, ruled by salvage crews.")` |
| `CHANGE_FIRST_ACTION` | `effectChangeFirstAction` | Rewrites `firstInput`, before the first turn. | `iw.TriggerEffect(type=iw.EffectType.CHANGE_FIRST_ACTION, data="I wake to alarms.")` |
| `CHANGE_VICTORY_CONDITION` | `effectChangeVictoryCondition` | Replaces the victory condition. | `iw.TriggerEffect(type=iw.EffectType.CHANGE_VICTORY_CONDITION, data={"condition": "I reach the lighthouse", "text": "You made it."})` |
| `CHANGE_DEFEAT_CONDITION` | `effectChangeDefeatCondition` | Replaces the defeat condition. | `iw.TriggerEffect(type=iw.EffectType.CHANGE_DEFEAT_CONDITION, data={"condition": "the crew all die", "text": "Nobody came home."})` |
| `CHANGE_PC_NAME` | `effectChangePCName` | Renames the playing character. | `iw.TriggerEffect(type=iw.EffectType.CHANGE_PC_NAME, data="The Stranger")` |
| `CHANGE_PC_DESCRIPTION` | `effectChangePCDescription` | Rewrites the playing character's description. | `iw.TriggerEffect(type=iw.EffectType.CHANGE_PC_DESCRIPTION, data="Scarred, quiet, unwilling to explain the coat.")` |
| `CHANGE_PC_SKILL` | `effectChangePCSkill` | Raises (`increase=True`) or lowers a skill by `amount`, clamped at `minmax`. | `iw.TriggerEffect(type=iw.EffectType.CHANGE_PC_SKILL, data={"name": "Nerve", "amount": 1, "minmax": 5, "increase": True})` |
| `SET_TRACKED_ITEM_VALUE` | `effectSetTrackedItemValue` | Writes a tracked item. `data` is `{action, newValue, replaceWith, trackedItemID}`; the `action` decides how — see `TrackedItemAction`. | `set_tracked_item(mood, "uneasy")` |
| `RUN_SCRIPT` | `effectRunScript` | Runs a `$`-script block. | `iw.TriggerEffect(type=iw.EffectType.RUN_SCRIPT, data="for each $m in $roster.party\n  $m.hp += 5")` |
| `FIRE_RANDOM_TRIGGER` | `effectFireRandomTrigger` | Fires one of the listed triggers at random. | `iw.TriggerEffect(type=iw.EffectType.FIRE_RANDOM_TRIGGER, data=[ambush.id, storm.id])` |
| `MODIFY_KEYWORD_BLOCK` | `effectModifyKeywordBlock` | The same for a lorebook entry, and rewrites its keywords too. | `iw.TriggerEffect(type=iw.EffectType.MODIFY_KEYWORD_BLOCK, data={"id": dragons.id, "content": "They are awake now.", "keywords": ["dragon", "wyrm"]})` |
| `ENDS_GAME` | `effectEndsGame` | Ends the game. `data` is the `can_continue` value — `False` is a hard ending. | `iw.TriggerEffect(type=iw.EffectType.ENDS_GAME, data=False)` |
| `MODIFY_TRACKED_ITEM_DETAILS` | `effectModifyTrackedItemDetails` | Changes an item's own name / description / visibility / update instructions. Each field you change needs its `override*` flag set alongside it. | `iw.TriggerEffect(type=iw.EffectType.MODIFY_TRACKED_ITEM_DETAILS, data={"trackedItemID": mood.id, "overrideName": True, "name": "Temper"})` |
| `PRESENT_CHOICE` | `effectPresentChoice` | Offers the player a choice; the picked value(s) land in the target item. | `iw.TriggerEffect(type=iw.EffectType.PRESENT_CHOICE, data={"message": "Which way?", "choices": "Left\nRight", "selectionMode": "single", "valueDelimiter": "newline", "minSelections": 1, "maxSelections": 1, "targetTrackedItemId": mood.id})` |
| `REQUEST_INPUT` | `effectRequestInput` | Prompts the player for text; the reply lands in the target item. | `iw.TriggerEffect(type=iw.EffectType.REQUEST_INPUT, data={"inputMode": "single", "requestText": "Name yourself.", "requiresInput": True, "targetTrackedItemId": mood.id})` |

`minSelections`/`maxSelections` come back as ints from some triggers and strings from others — read both.

### `ConditionType`

| member | value in the JSON | what it does | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ON_TURN` | `triggerOnTurn` | Fires on turn **≥ N**, not exactly N. `data=1` is the "every turn" idiom. | `iw.TriggerCondition(type=iw.ConditionType.ON_TURN, category="condition", data=1)` |
| `ON_EVENT` | `triggerOnEvent` | Fires when the AI judges the described situation to have happened. | `iw.TriggerCondition(type=iw.ConditionType.ON_EVENT, category="condition", data="the crew mutinies")` |
| `ON_CHARACTER` | `triggerOnCharacter` | Gates on who the player picked. | `iw.TriggerCondition(type=iw.ConditionType.ON_CHARACTER, category="condition", data=[hero.characterId])` |
| `ON_TRACKED_ITEM` | `triggerOnTrackedItem` | Reads a tracked item. `data` is `{inequality, requiredValue, trackedItemID, textComparison}`. `textComparison` is **required** (`"contains"` / `"does_not_contain"`) — a condition without it is dropped on import. Text items have *no* exact match, only contains. `tracked_item_is` fills it in for you. | `tracked_item_is(mood, "uneasy")` |
| `ON_RANDOM_CHANCE` | `triggerOnRandomChance` | Fires that percent of the time. The percentage is a **string**. | `iw.TriggerCondition(type=iw.ConditionType.ON_RANDOM_CHANCE, category="condition", data="37")` |
| `ON_PAW_SCRIPT` | `triggerOnPawScript` | Fires when a `$`-expression is true. | `iw.TriggerCondition(type=iw.ConditionType.ON_PAW_SCRIPT, category="condition", data="$roster.party.count()>0")` |
| `PREREQS` | `triggerPrereqs` | Fires only once the listed triggers have. | `iw.TriggerCondition(type=iw.ConditionType.PREREQS, category="condition", data=[ambush.id])` |

Every leaf condition carries `category="condition"`; the helpers set it for you. A **logic group** is a
condition with no `type` at all — `category="logic"` and an `operator` — whose `data` is a list of
sub-conditions. It nests arbitrarily, and its `TriggerEvent` needs `advancedLogic=True`:

```python
iw.TriggerCondition(category="logic", operator=iw.LogicOperator.OR, data=[
    tracked_item_is(mood, "uneasy"),
    tracked_item_is(crew, "2", inequality=iw.Inequality.AT_MOST),
])
```

### `LogicOperator`

| member | value in the JSON | what it does | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AND` | `and` | Every sub-condition must hold. | `iw.TriggerCondition(category="logic", operator=iw.LogicOperator.AND, data=[tracked_item_is(mood, "uneasy"), tracked_item_is(crew, "2", inequality=iw.Inequality.AT_MOST)])` |
| `OR` | `or` | Any sub-condition may hold. | `iw.TriggerCondition(category="logic", operator=iw.LogicOperator.OR, data=[tracked_item_is(mood, "uneasy"), tracked_item_is(mood, "afraid")])` |

## The functions

### `reset_ids(seed: int = 0) -> None`

Reset the shared ID generator. Ids are drawn from one seeded sequence, so a world's ids depend on everything generated before it in the same process. Call this before building a world to make its output reproducible no matter what else was built first (the build script does).

## Initial values: `same` / `character` / `player`

A tracked item's `initialValueBasedOnPC` picks where its starting value comes from. The three modes put
that value in three *different places*, which is the part worth knowing:

| mode | the UI's wording | where the value lives |
|---|---|---|
| `SAME` | initial value is always the same | the item's own `initialValue` |
| `CHARACTER` | depends on which character the player chooses | one entry per character under `possibleCharacters[].initialTrackedItemValues`; the item's own `initialValue` stays empty |
| `PLAYER` | can be entered by the player | the item's own `initialValue`, acting as the default the player edits |

Both `PLAYER` and `CHARACTER` can offer the player a **list to choose from** instead of free text — given
either literally or as a `$`-script yielding the options — but each mode carries it on a different object,
and the near-identical field names are easy to mix up:

| | literal choices | script yielding choices | the value itself |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PLAYER` — on the **item** | `initialValueChoices` | `initialValueChoicesScript` | `initialValue` (the default selection) |
| `CHARACTER` — on the **per-character entry** | `initialPCValue` *as a list* | `initialPCValueChoicesScript` | `initialPCValue` |

Per-character entries are not free-form overrides you attach at will: a character carries **one entry per
`CHARACTER`-mode item**, and the entry's own `initialValueBasedOnPC` mirrors the item's. An entry declaring
any other mode has no item it can belong to and is dropped on import.

## Scripting & structured data

The engine has a `$`-expression scripting language and structured (YAML) tracked items. `iw` models the
enum values and passes the script text through verbatim; the language itself is the engine's.
`TrackedItemDataType.YAML` holds the document, `ConditionType.ON_PAW_SCRIPT` reads an expression, and
`EffectType.RUN_SCRIPT` runs a block. The `TrackedItem` fields the feature needs — `variableName`,
`enforceFormat`, `formatSchema`, `formatExample`, `driftAcknowledgedForName`, and the two
`initialValueChoices*` fields — all default to `None` and strip from output unless set, so worlds
predating the feature serialise unchanged.

## IDs & helpers

Objects that need an id get one from a shared, deterministic `IDGenerator`, and **nothing in this repo
ever writes one by hand**. `World.from_dict` re-seeds it from the parsed data so ids created afterwards
cannot collide with the parsed world's. `iw.reset_ids()` makes a build reproducible regardless of what was
built before it (the build script calls it).

`set_tracked_item(item, value, action=SET)` and `tracked_item_is(item, value, inequality=IS_EXACTLY)`
build the effect that writes a tracked item and the condition that reads one. **Use them.** The engine's
payload for both carries the item's id *twice* — inside `data`, and again in the sibling `trackedItemID`
field — and nothing checks that the two copies agree; a world whose copies disagree loads perfectly and
silently never fires. Both take the item itself, or a raw id string for engine built-ins like
`turn_number` that are not items in your world.

## Notes

- Dataclasses use **identity** equality and hashing (`eq=False`), so instances are hashable and can be
  used as dict keys (which is how `plot` keys its stage maps). Two instances with identical fields are
  **not** equal — compare `.to_dict()` if you need value equality.
- Parsing is strict on purpose: an unknown field raises `NotImplementedError` rather than being dropped,
  so the dataclasses cannot quietly fall behind the engine's schema.
